description: The Boston Globe’s Tiana Woodard spoke to Urban College of Boston President Dr. Yves Salomon- Fernández about the recent US Census Bureau data and the racial wealth gap. ...
content:
Recently released U.S. Census Bureau data revealed that over the past year, Black income rose 12% and Asian American income increased 7% across the city and state, while Hispanic median income fell 2%. Yet white families in Boston remain the only group with a median household income exceeding $100,000.

The report quantified what many of the households Urban College serves already feel: the racial income gap persists despite widespread income gains, because income doesn't always translate into wealth. The Boston Globe's Tiana Woodard spoke with Urban College President Dr. Yves Salomon-Fernández about closing those gaps. “People might look at it and say, ‘Oh, it's just 2 percent,'” she noted. “But a 2 percent decrease over time can become really significant.”

As a Hispanic-Serving Institution serving nontraditional students, Urban College is uniquely positioned to help Black, Latino, and Asian American households build professional careers and generational wealth. Recognizing that college debt hampers low-income students, the college has committed to a low- to no-debt model—helping students of color access the tools to build individual and family wealth.

description: Urban College of Boston is pleased to announce its receipt of a significant Workforce Development Grant from the Massachusetts Life Sciences Center (MLSC), as part of a recent funding initiative total...
content:
Urban College of Boston is pleased to announce its receipt of a significant Workforce Development Grant from the Massachusetts Life Sciences Center (MLSC), part of a funding initiative totaling over $13 million. The award places Urban College among twenty institutions funded to advance life sciences, workforce development, and STEM education.

The grant will support the development and launch of Urban College's Science Simulation Laboratory & Curriculum (SSLC) Program, establishing a state-of-the-art simulation laboratory on the college's Chinatown campus. As a designated Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution (AANAPISI), Urban College is committed to fostering opportunities for underserved communities.

The funding will bolster the college's Science and Technology curriculum—particularly for associate-degree students—addressing critical skills gaps and meeting the growing demands of Massachusetts' life-sciences sector. The new lab will provide practical, hands-on experience and advance the college's mission to open new pathways to opportunity through individualized, supportive education.

title: Urban College Blog | Urban College of Boston
description: Boston, MA, 6/26/2024 – Urban College of Boston is proud to announce the addition of two distinguished individuals to its Board of Trustees. Dr. Constanza Cabello and Dr. Jan Wyatt bring a wealth of e...
content:
Urban College of Boston announced the addition of two distinguished individuals to its Board of Trustees, reinforcing the college's commitment to equal opportunity in higher education.

Dr. Constanza Cabello is a diversity, equity, and inclusion leader who serves as Vice President for Equity Programs at State Street Corporation. Previously a senior diversity and community-engagement officer in higher education, she founded Cabello Consulting LLC in 2011. She holds a Doctorate of Education in Organizational Leadership Studies from Northeastern University, a Master of Science in Counseling from Central Connecticut State University, and a Bachelor of Science from the University of Connecticut.

Dr. Jan Wyatt brings more than eighteen years of higher-education leadership experience, having served as professor, department chair, academic dean, vice provost, and now Vice President of Academic Programs at SNHU. He helped develop the award-winning Higher Education and Real-World Training (HEaRT) initiative and holds a Ph.D. in Organization and Management from Capella University and an M.B.A. from SNHU.

Board Chair Peter Ebb welcomed the new members: “Both have extensive experience in areas of critical importance to the College. Like many of Urban College's students, both were born outside the United States and have a deep understanding of the challenges our students face.” The college also thanked departing members Dr. Paul LeBlanc and Yiming Shuang for their contributions.
